pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine darkening to a deep port-wine color upon standing/light exposure, paired with the classic tetrad of severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam, autonomic instability, neuropsychiatric disturbances, and motor neuropathy triggered by fasting. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), the third enzyme in the heme biosynthetic pathway. Severe caloric restriction or fasting induces hepatic ALAS1 (via PGC-1alpha activation), leading to a massive upstream accumulation of neurotoxic porphyrin precursors: delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). These toxic precursors cause autonomic neuropathy (hypertension, tachycardia, severe abdominal colic), central nervous system dysfunction (psychosis, seizures, SIADH-induced hyponatremia), and peripheral motor neuropathy. PBG oxidizes and polymerizes into porphobilin and uroporphyrin when exposed to air and light, producing the characteristic dark port-wine coloration of the urine. Treatment requires immediate IV glucose or IV hemin to downregulate hepatic ALAS1.
